welcome.label: Welcome · The Duck Derby Flop

parts.label: 🦆 The Duck Derby
parts.title: 200 ducks, one pond
parts.body: A wave machine was supposed to push them to the dock.

parts.label: ❓ The question
parts.title: Will BIGGER waves work?
parts.body: Mr. Ortiz wants a giant wave machine next year.

parts.label: 🧪 Meet Dr. Nair
parts.title: Dr. Priya Nair
parts.body: A materials scientist: what things are made of and how they behave.

welcome.script:
(Hold up a rubber duck, or any small floating toy.) If I make waves in the bathtub, will this duck surf to the other end?

[ON SCREEN: The Duck Derby]
That is exactly what the town of Palmetto Springs tried: two hundred ducks and a wave machine.

[ON SCREEN: A real duck race]
This is a real duck race. Look closely at where these ducks are floating.

[ON SCREEN: The question]
Not one duck reached the dock! Now the organizer wants bigger waves.

[ON SCREEN: Meet Dr. Nair]
Our new scientist, Dr. Priya Nair, needs your help. Read her case file just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · be the crowd (Clue 1)

parts.label: 🏟️ Be the crowd
parts.title: Do the wave
rows: Tap Section 1, then each glowing section
Watch the fan in the red cap

warmup.script:
(Stand up fast with your arms in the air, then sit back down.) That’s one fan doing the wave. Now picture a whole stadium!

[ON SCREEN: Be the crowd]
You’re in charge of the crowd. Tap Section one, then each glowing section, in order. Don’t wait too long!

[ON SCREEN: Think about it]
Keep your eye on the fan in the red cap. When the wave goes all the way around, where is she? Then write about a wave you’ve seen.

part1.label: Part 1 · same wave, new stuff (Clue 2)

parts.label: 🔴 Tag it
parts.title: Tag one piece red
parts.body: Send a wave. Where does your tag end up?

part1.script:
(Tie a ribbon, or a twist tie, onto a jump rope or a string, and flick one end.) Watch the ribbon. Does it travel to the other end?

[ON SCREEN: Tag it]
In this game you tag one piece red, then send a wave, and watch your tag.

[ON SCREEN: Same wave, new stuff]
Try all five: a slinky, a rope, pond water, a line of kids and even air. Your wave log fills in. Then watch for a surprise about the duck.

part2.label: Part 2 · measure the waves (Clue 3)

parts.label: 📏 Measure the waves
parts.title: Lay a bracket
rows: Amplitude: center line up to a crest
Wavelength: crest to the next crest

part2.script:
(Hold one hand flat for the center line and lift the other hand above it.) From the middle up to the top: that’s the amplitude.

[ON SCREEN: Measure the waves]
Tap two dots to lay a bracket and read how many squares it is. Measure the amplitude, then the wavelength, for three waves. Which one carries the most energy?

explore.label: Part 3 · shake it yourself (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🌊 Shake it yourself
parts.title: Your hand makes the wave
rows: Drag the hand up and down
Watch the cups and the red ribbon

explore.script:
(Wiggle your hand gently, then hard, like shaking a rope.) Small wiggle. BIG wiggle. What do you think changes?

[ON SCREEN: Shake it yourself]
Drag the hand at the end of the slinky up and down, or press Gentle wiggle. Watch the red ribbon and the tower of cups at the far end. Then try a hard wiggle. Your log fills in, so compare the two.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Will bigger waves work?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Three places to work
rows: Make or find a wave, then draw and label it

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You have four clues. Will a bigger wave machine get the ducks to the dock? Pick the answer that fits every clue. Then watch for a twist, and help Mr. Ortiz fix his plan.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next: two short answers. For Part C, make a wave with a jump rope or a string, or think of one you’ve seen. Then sketch and label it. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “When a wave moves through water, the water has to travel with it.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Make a wave with your arm and pretend to ride it.) Does the water ride along with the wave?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says the water has to travel with the wave. Think about the duck’s little loop and the red tag.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🦆 Your specimen
parts.title: A derby duck
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next lesson
parts.title: Coded messages
parts.body: Send a secret message with light and sound.

closing.script:
(Set the duck down and give it a little bob.) Bob, bob. Still right here!

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and a derby duck goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next lesson]
Next time: waves can carry messages, too. You’ll design your own secret code with light and sound.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
